title: Regulatory format-spec (ADR-0009, FR-02)
description: Meta-schema for a class-parameterized regulatory format spec (e.g. skills/REGULATORY/IEC-62304/spec.json). A regime instance declares its required sections and a conformance checklist; class-gating is a data-driven filter (required_for_classes), never a per-class schema fork. `fillable` on every section and `section` on every checklist entry are structural invariants (C-3): omitting either fails validation so a permissive default can never be assumed.

id.description: Regime identifier, e.g. 'IEC-62304'. Used verbatim as <spec> in the gap-line template.

edition.description: The pinned edition/date of the regulatory document, e.g. '2006+A1:2015'.

classification_axis.description: Ordered set of software safety classes this regime gates on, e.g. ['A','B','C'].

id.description: Stable section identifier. MUST describe the regulatory requirement (e.g. 'design-development-record-set'), never a hardcoded customer-document token such as 'DHF'.

spec_ref.description: Bare section-number reference within the regime document, e.g. '5.3' (no leading section-symbol — the gap-line template supplies '§' itself).

required_for_classes.description: Subset of classification_axis for which this section is required. A class-gate filter reads this list; it is never expressed as a separate per-class schema.

field_constraints.description: Free-form structural constraints on the section's expected fields. Data, not enforced by this meta-schema beyond being an object.

cross_references.description: Other standards/sections this section cross-references, e.g. ['ISO-14971:2019'].

fillable.description: Structural invariant (C-3, RK-01/RK-02): false means the reformatter's single write path (_emit_section) may NEVER populate this slot with generated content, regardless of what appears in the source — always a gap line and a marked, empty slot. Required so a section can never omit it and fall back to a permissive default.

section.description: The required_sections[].id this checklist rule evaluates. Required (C-3, AC-02.3): a checklist entry with no section is unenforceable and must be rejected.
